12gong.brief: Elder Gong teaches that temple covenants bind families together forever, and invites us to bring a temple culture of our own: coming often, sacrificing gladly and serving with gratitude.

lists.principle: Temple sealings rest on three truths about how God works: He wants us home together, He honors our choices, and His Spirit makes covenants binding.

items.description: Heavenly Father's whole purpose is to bring us back to Him as families, happy and for eternity.
items.quote: Heavenly Father’s work and glory is for us to return to Him, united as families, happy and forever.

items.description: We chose God's plan, and He will never force anyone into an eternal relationship they do not choose.
items.quote: God will not require a woman or man to be sealed or live in an eternal relationship he or she does not choose.

items.description: When the Spirit confirms that our ordinances were done rightly and our covenants kept, they bind in time and eternity.
items.quote: When the Holy Spirit of Promise witnesses and confirms the efficacy of ordinances and covenants, they become binding in time and eternity.

lists.principle: The temple blesses us most when we bring a temple culture of our own to it, not only when one is built near us.

items.description: Announcements, groundbreakings and dedications are milestones; the blessings begin when we come.
items.quote: First, a temple dedication is a beginning.

items.description: With temples closer, the old spirit of sacrifice shows in coming more often, bringing family names and serving.
items.quote: we can manifest the precious spirit of temple sacrifice in new ways. We can come to the temple more often.

items.description: Whatever its size or setting, every temple points to the Savior.
items.quote: everything in each temple testifies of Jesus Christ

items.description: The temple is a sacred privilege, so we come grateful and patient.
items.quote: Fourth, temple sacrifice and temple service include a spirit of gratitude.

items.description: Saving for and caring for our own temple clothes shows our children that we love the Lord and our covenants.
items.quote: please consider saving for and buying your own ceremonial temple clothes

13runia.brief: Sister Runia teaches that hard experiences are part of a loving Father's plan to make us like Him, and that when we invite the Savior in, He shapes us into what only He knows we can become.

lists.principle: God's promises to the obedient are true, but they are not an umbrella that keeps every storm away; the gospel is the rock we stand on during the storm.

items.description: Obedience brings blessings, a promise she grew up hearing and still calls true.
items.quote: If you keep the commandments, you’ll be blessed.

items.description: The Lord opens the windows of heaven to those who pay tithing.
items.quote: Pay your tithing, and the windows of heaven will open.

items.description: Keeping the Word of Wisdom brings health and protection, though it does not shield us from every trial.
items.quote: Follow the Word of Wisdom, and you’ll have health and protection.

lists.principle: Each life is its own story, written with care and written for a reason.

items.description: Your story is your own, so there is no need to measure it against anyone else's.
items.quote: Your story is personal. So you don’t need to look sideways and ask, “How come my life doesn’t look like theirs?”

items.description: What you live through has meaning, and even suffering is not wasted.
items.quote: And it’s purposeful in that it has meaning. Our suffering means something.

lists.principle: One day we will thank the Savior for all that shaped us, even the pain, because it helped us become more like Him.

items.description: Once invited, the Savior begins His work in us, and it can feel abrupt and aggressive.
items.quote: Then He will start carving, sometimes surprising us with how abrupt and aggressive the work feels.

items.description: God is forming us into something we cannot yet see but He already knows.
items.quote: God is shaping us into something only He knows we can become.

items.description: A godlike life is carved from what hurts, both what happens to us and righteous desires not yet fulfilled.
items.quote: And a godlike life is carved from the very things that make it hard—the gut-wrenching things that happen and the righteous desires that haven’t.

items.description: Our refining trials come precisely because God loves us.
items.quote: It is precisely because He loves us that we’re having these tempering, refining experiences.

14causse.brief: Elder Caussé teaches that every disciple, not only apostles, is called to bear witness of Jesus Christ, and that a simple, sincere testimony shared with love carries the Spirit's power to change lives.

lists.principle: A testimony is a personal gift from God that grows as we trust it, seek, live the gospel and feel the Holy Ghost.

items.description: We trust and nurture our own testimony, even when it differs from someone else's.
items.quote: Please trust it, nurture it, and bear it, because it is uniquely yours.

items.description: Those who sincerely seek truth have been changed by the witness of humble servants of the Lord.
items.quote: Throughout history, countless seekers of truth have been transformed by the testimonies of humble servants of the Lord

items.description: Our testimony shows in what we do as well as what we say.
items.quote: Through your testimonies, in word and deed, you demonstrate the reality of a loving Savior

items.thing: The quiet influence of the Holy Ghost
items.description: It is the Spirit, not our words, that confirms what is true.
items.quote: it is the Spirit—not words—that testifies of the truth

lists.principle: A testimony carries power because it is true and confirmed by the Spirit, not because it is long, polished or dramatic.

items.description: A minute or two of sincere witness can make a profound difference.
items.quote: A brief and sincere expression of faith can make a profound difference

items.description: Humble servants with simple words still carry divine power when the Holy Ghost confirms them.
items.quote: Their words may be simple and their speech imperfect, but their witness carries divine power because it is confirmed by the Holy Ghost.

items.description: Even two simple sentences of belief are enough, if we mean them.
items.quote: I was so nervous that I only managed to say two simple sentences: ‘I know that God loves me’ and ‘I know that God has a plan for me.’

lists.skip: A sweep of names in one sentence; the talk says nothing of Enoch, Moses or Joseph Smith individually, only the shared pattern

lists.principle: We can bear witness of Jesus Christ almost anywhere, briefly and naturally, as the Holy Ghost prompts.

items.description: A short, sincere word of faith at home can make a lasting difference.
items.quote: whether at home with your family

items.description: Testimony meetings are a natural place to share what we know.
items.quote: in testimony meetings

items.description: Ministering and teaching give us chances to testify of the Savior.
items.quote: in ministering visits and missionary lessons

items.description: Our witness can be shared online as well as in person.
items.quote: on social media

items.description: Simple, natural words in ordinary moments are a testimony too.
items.quote: You can share your beliefs in simple and natural ways, such as “I love our Savior, Jesus Christ” or “The gospel brings joy to my heart.”

15sikahema.brief: Elder Sikahema teaches that living prophets, seers and revelators are a precious gift restored through Joseph Smith, and that we should never hold the oracles of God as a light thing.

lists.principle: After centuries without revelation to prophets, the Lord restored what had been lost through the Prophet Joseph Smith.

items.description: The restored gospel revealed truths that had long been withheld.
items.quote: the gospel restored by Joseph Smith revealed truths previously withheld from them

items.description: Joseph restored the Savior's Church with prophets, seers and revelators who hold priesthood keys.
items.quote: Joseph helped restore the Savior’s Church with prophets, seers, and revelators who held priesthood keys that would one day bind them together as a family forever.

items.description: Apostles hold the authority for ordinances that seal families for eternity.
items.quote: held the authority for the ordinances that would later seal them as an eternal family

items.description: The Lord's revelations to Joseph became the Doctrine and Covenants, published despite early objections.
items.quote: the Lord’s revelations through the Prophet Joseph that would eventually become the Doctrine and Covenants

items.thing: Knowledge of God's plan of salvation
items.description: Understanding of Heavenly Father's plan was restored or rediscovered through Joseph.
items.quote: knowledge of God’s plan of salvation would all be restored or rediscovered through the Prophet Joseph Smith

16hathaway.brief: Elder Hathaway teaches that Jesus Christ is the Great Deliverer, whose deliverance from every affliction is certain and comes through a scriptural pattern, in His own time and way.

lists.principle: Jesus Christ, who suffered afflictions of every kind, can deliver the righteous from the ordinary sorrows of mortal life.

items.description: The Savior understands the loneliness of being left out.
items.quote: felt left out

items.description: He can deliver us from doubts about our own worth.
items.quote: wondered if you were enough

items.description: He comprehends grief and can heal those who mourn.
items.quote: lost someone you loved

items.description: Sickness is among the afflictions He knows how to succor.
items.quote: faced illness

items.description: Trouble at home is not beyond His reach.
items.quote: experienced family difficulties

items.thing: A burden no one else can see
items.description: He sees and can lift the burdens we carry silently.
items.quote: carried a burden no one else could see

lists.principle: The Savior's deliverance follows a pattern seen in scripture, leading from hard questions to His certain help in His own time.

items.description: Hard questions and deep feelings are not sin; they are a moment to choose to turn toward Christ.
items.quote: Such questions and emotions are not sin or weakness; they can create a sacred space where agency is activated and we choose whether to turn toward Jesus Christ.

items.description: As we seek Him and keep our covenants, the Savior visits us with assurances of deliverance.
items.quote: As we humbly and patiently keep our covenants, the Savior will visit us in our afflictions and bring assurances of deliverance.

items.description: His grace does not remove the pain but gives us strength beyond our own.
items.quote: This grace does not remove the pain and difficulty of affliction; it is an enabling power that allows us, after all we can do, to receive divine strength beyond our own

items.thing: Deliverance in His time and way
items.description: The Savior delivers us and consecrates our afflictions for our gain, on His timetable.
items.quote: the Savior delivers us from our afflictions and consecrates them for our gain. He does this in His time and way.

lists.principle: Sincere seeking means turning toward Heavenly Father and Jesus Christ, and these acts of faith draw us closer to Him.

items.description: Like Alma's people in bondage, we cry to God from the heart.
items.quote: Alma’s people in bondage “began to cry mightily to God.”

items.description: King Darius fasted through the night while waiting for Daniel's deliverance.
items.quote: King Darius fasted through the night as he waited for Daniel’s deliverance from the lions’ den.

items.description: Studying the scriptures is another way we turn toward God in our trials.
items.quote: turning toward Heavenly Father and Jesus Christ through heartfelt prayer, purposeful fasting, and scripture study

lists.skip: Three words naming how Kenzie binds herself to God, not developed; prayer repeats c-13 and only covenant keeping has words of its own

lists.principle: The Lord has not forgotten us while we wait; His deliverance is certain.

items.description: Waiting can bring converting growth that an earlier rescue might not.
items.quote: He knows that lessons learned while waiting can bring converting growth that an earlier rescue might not produce.

items.description: The Lord's attention has not wandered from us.
items.quote: He has not forgotten you.

items.description: He will deliver; the only question is how and when.
items.quote: His deliverance is certain; the question for most righteous followers is not if He will deliver but how and when He will do so.

lists.principle: Jesus Christ will deliver us, though His miracles come on different timelines.

items.description: Sometimes the Savior's deliverance comes right away.
items.quote: Some miracles are immediate

items.description: While we wait on the Lord in faith, growth and spiritual stretching come before deliverance.
items.quote: As we wait upon the Lord and exercise faith in Him, needed growth and spiritual stretching come

items.description: Even death does not place us beyond His power, as Jairus learned.
items.quote: showing that no mortal timeline can place us beyond Christ’s power to deliver

17soares.brief: Elder Soares teaches that a higher and holier fast, joined with prayer and generous fast offerings, draws us nearer to the Lord, turns our hearts to His children and opens us to the blessings Isaiah promised.

lists.skip: Four general blessings named once in the opening; the talk develops its blessings in the later lists (c-9, c-30, c-35)

lists.principle: Isaiah promised those who fast that the Lord would bring light, healing and His near presence.

items.description: Light breaks into the life of the one who fasts faithfully.
items.quote: Then shall thy light break forth as the morning

items.description: Health and renewal come quickly to those who keep the fast.
items.quote: thine health shall spring forth speedily

items.thing: The Lord is near when we call
items.description: When we call on the Lord, He answers and is close.
items.quote: Then shalt thou call, and the Lord shall answer; thou shalt cry, and he shall say, Here I am.

lists.principle: A fast offering is more than money; it shows the heart and faith of the one who gives it.

items.description: Freely given, even a small offering becomes consecrated compassion and service.
items.quote: Though our fast offerings may seem small and simple, they become consecrated expressions of compassion, concern, and service.

items.thing: Faith in the Lord Jesus Christ
items.description: Our giving follows the Savior, who came down to succor His people.
items.quote: This spirit of generosity also reflects the Savior’s own example.

items.description: Fast offerings are how we help free the oppressed and lift burdens today.
items.quote: our desire to help “the oppressed go free” and “break every yoke,” as the Lord taught through the prophet Isaiah, finds tangible expression in generous fast offerings

lists.principle: The blessings of fasting usually come quietly and tenderly, changing us from within.

items.description: Fasting and prayer soften our hearts and open us to the Holy Ghost.
items.quote: Our hearts are softened, our souls become more receptive to the influence of the Holy Ghost

items.description: Faith, love and devotion to the Lord deepen as we fast and pray.
items.quote: Through the union of fasting and prayer, our faith, love, and devotion to Him deepen.

items.description: Through the fast the Lord makes us holy and pours out His Spirit.
items.quote: Through this divinely appointed practice, the Lord will sanctify us and pour His Spirit and blessings more abundantly into our lives.

items.description: He promises that miracles will come to those who embrace the fast's divine purpose.
items.quote: I promise, in the name of our Savior, Jesus Christ, that miracles will come into your life.

lists.principle: Living the law of the fast in a higher and holier way brings us closer to the Savior and to others.

items.description: Joyful fasting with prayer and generosity brings sweeter, more personal communion with the Lord.
items.quote: Fasting, when observed with joy and joined with prayer and generosity, brings sweeter communion with the Lord and a deeper, more personal connection with Him.

items.description: Fasting and prayer draw heaven near and give power to overcome or endure.
items.quote: they draw heaven near and endow us with divine power to overcome or endure whatever circumstances we may face

items.thing: Sensitive to the needs of others
items.description: Following the Savior's example of succor opens our hearts to others.
items.quote: As we follow His perfect example by seeking to succor God’s children, our hearts are opened to the needs of others

18douglas.brief: Bishop Douglas thanks missionaries for the most important work they could be doing and invites the rising generation, including new converts, to place full-time missionary service high on their list.

lists.principle: Missionaries are not only messengers but living examples of the message they carry.

items.description: Missionaries carry a testimony of Jesus Christ that can bless a suffering world.
items.quote: You have a testimony of Jesus Christ and His Atonement that can bless a world suffering without knowledge of His divine mission.

items.description: Their desire to serve is why they radiate the Light of Christ and teach with power.
items.quote: it’s why they radiate the Light of Christ and teach with convincing power

items.description: Like the sons of Mosiah, they cannot bear for any soul to perish.
items.quote: were desirous that salvation should be declared to every creature, for they could not bear that any human soul should perish

items.description: Missionaries of all ages find great joy in serving among Heavenly Father's children.
items.quote: Record numbers of missionaries of all ages are finding great joy as they humbly dedicate themselves to serving the Lord

lists.skip: Five things set aside, named once in one sentence; the talk says nothing more about each

19christofferson.brief: President Christofferson teaches that gambling is morally wrong and harmful, and pleads with us to live on a higher plane, using the time and money we save to do good.

lists.principle: The smartphone has put gambling in our pockets, and three new online markets are driving its explosive growth.

items.description: Wagers placed online on sports scores, statistics or events.
items.quote: First is online sports betting, which involves wagers on sports scores, statistics, or events.

items.description: Internet versions of slots, roulette, blackjack and poker, sometimes called iGaming.
items.quote: Second is online casino-type games, sometimes referred to as internet or iGaming

items.description: A newer platform for betting on whether and when almost anything will happen.
items.quote: A third, relatively new platform is what are called “prediction markets” that allow participants to bet on whether something will or will not happen and when.

lists.skip: Examples of casino games given in passing, not counsel a reader would want as a list

lists.principle: Youth and young adults are especially vulnerable to the pull of gambling.

items.description: For the young, betting can quickly become consuming and compulsive.
items.quote: It easily becomes consuming and often compulsive.

items.description: When everyone seems to accept gambling, the pull grows stronger.
items.quote: Widespread social acceptance only adds to the enticement.

items.description: Many begin gambling as children, and the numbers rise with age.
items.quote: In the United States, 36 percent of boys age 11 to 17 reported gambling last year

items.description: Smartphones make gambling available all the time, in private, almost anywhere.
items.quote: an activity available continuously, privately, and almost anywhere

items.description: Aggressive marketing compounds the other pressures young people face.
items.quote: early exposure, easy online access, and intense marketing

lists.skip: Three nouns in one sentence, not developed; the same costs (time, relationships) are covered more fully in c-26
A journalist's quoted litany of six nouns; nothing in the talk develops them one by one

lists.principle: Every choice has an opportunity cost, and gambling costs far more than the money wagered.

items.description: The gambling industry profits only when its customers lose.
items.quote: the industry’s entire business model is built on its customers losing money

items.description: Time spent gambling is time lost for something better.
items.quote: if we spend time doing one thing, we lose the opportunity to do another

items.description: Constant access can turn casual betting into a habit with far-reaching family and social costs.
items.quote: continuous, mobile access can transform occasional entertainment into repeated behavior that displaces saving, increases debt, and creates far-reaching family and social costs

items.description: He pleads that we use the time and resources saved to do good.
items.quote: my plea again is not only to refrain from gambling but to use the time and resources saved thereby for doing good

lists.principle: A life well-lived builds up others through honest, productive work, while gambling leads the opposite way.

items.description: A good life adds to the well-being of the people around us.
items.quote: A key part of a life well-lived is contributing to the well-being of others.

items.description: We spend our lives producing something of worth.
items.quote: It is being productive in worthy endeavors.

items.description: Our gain should never come at someone else's loss.
items.quote: It is being and doing better without others doing worse.

items.description: A good life supports honest work, which leads to just and prosperous societies.
items.quote: It comes by supporting and rewarding work rather than idle pursuits.

21renlund.brief: Elder Renlund teaches that when daily trials loom, we can look past our “cold oatmeal,” remember what the Lord has already done, and trust His promises, which apply to each of us.

lists.principle: The bigger picture keeps small trials in their place: looking back at God's goodness and forward to His promises.

items.description: Remembering the great things the Lord has already done for us steadies our trust in hard days.
items.quote: As we reflect on the great things the Lord has already done and remember His goodness and mercy, we are better positioned to grasp the bigger picture

items.description: His promises reach ahead of us, and there is no asterisk that leaves any of us out.
items.quote: We can trust the Lord, especially His promises. These promises apply to you.

lists.principle: God had already worked miracle after miracle for ancient Israel, yet they kept focusing on their discomforts and their trust eroded.

items.description: When Israel was trapped with no way out, God delivered them.
items.quote: God saved them when they were trapped at the Red Sea

items.description: In the wilderness, the Lord provided what they lacked to stay alive.
items.quote: provided for them when they lacked food and water

items.description: Even when they grumbled about their monotonous food, the Lord still helped them by a miracle.
items.quote: Even when they complained about a monotonous diet, the Lord miraculously helped them.

lists.principle: When hard times make us doubt God, the answer is to trust Him and His promises, because none of us is the exception.

items.description: We may wonder whether His blessings are meant for us, but no one is excluded from them.
items.quote: there is no asterisk excluding you from God’s richest blessings

items.description: The Savior has made ample provision, enough to cover every need each of us has.
items.quote: there is more than enough to cover any breach, need, or deficit for all of us, for each of us.

items.thing: His capacity to keep His promises
items.description: The Lord has always reassured His people that He will not break His covenant with them.
items.quote: How often the Lord reassured the children of Israel, and reassures us, of His constancy, declaring, “I will never break my covenant with you.”

22farnes.brief: President Farnes teaches that taking the Savior's name means seeing people as He sees them, and that ministering with compassion to whomever God places in our path is simply what His followers do.

lists.principle: Divine appointments often come when we are stretched thin and unsure we have anything left to give.

items.description: He and his wife were raising a young family during this demanding season of service.
items.quote: We had five young children

items.description: He also carried the daily weight of running a business.
items.quote: a business to run

items.thing: A full day of Church meetings
items.description: That Saturday held meetings from early morning to a ward temple night, and he wondered if he had enough to give.
items.quote: a full day of Church meetings, starting at 8:00 a.m. and concluding with a ward temple night

lists.principle: Taking the Savior's name upon us is a choice to live as He does, so that His life is reflected in ours.

items.description: We look at the people around us the way the Savior looks at them.
items.quote: That means we choose to see as He sees

items.description: We let ourselves care about others the way He cares about them.
items.quote: feel as He feels

items.description: We act toward others as the Savior would act.
items.quote: and do as He would do. His life should be reflected in ours.

lists.principle: When people meet a disciple of Jesus Christ, they should experience something of the Savior Himself.

items.description: With His Spirit, we can minister with the Savior's loving kindness.
items.quote: we can minister as the Savior would, with His power and His loving kindness.

items.description: Others should feel the Savior's patience in how we treat them.
items.quote: His patience

items.description: Others should sense in us the hope that the Savior offers.
items.quote: His hope

items.description: Others should feel the Savior's love through us.
items.quote: His love

items.description: For Christ, compassion was something He did, not only something He felt.
items.quote: We often think of compassion as something we feel, but for Christ, it was something He did.

lists.principle: In the parable of the good Samaritan, ministering follows a simple pattern: we see, we feel compassion, and we act.

items.description: Where others saw an interruption, the Samaritan saw a person in need.
items.quote: Seeing awakened compassion.

items.description: What he felt for the wounded traveler moved him to do something.
items.quote: Compassion moved him to act.

items.description: His actions changed the traveler's life.
items.quote: And his actions changed a life forever.

lists.skip: Three nouns in one phrase about the Savior's ministry, with nothing said of each.

lists.principle: A divine appointment rarely asks much of us; it asks us to notice, to care and to act.

items.thing: See the person God placed in our path
items.description: We look up and notice the person God has put in front of us.
items.quote: All we had to do was see the person God had placed in our path

items.description: We see that person with compassion rather than judging them.
items.quote: look with compassion rather than judgment

items.description: We turn compassion into action and minister to the person before us.
items.quote: Let us put compassion into action and minister to the person in front of us.

23chigbundu.brief: Elder Chigbundu teaches that small and simple things build a spiritual immunity that helps us face the challenges of life with strength and without fear.

lists.skip: Three bare nouns naming the troubles of our time, with nothing said of each.

lists.principle: Small and simple things, done consistently, build our spiritual immunity and arm us against the adversary.

items.description: Daily, meaningful study helps us know the Lord and strengthens our faith against temptation and trouble.
items.quote: Daily, meaningful scripture study invites the guidance of the Holy Ghost and builds our faith to face the temptations and the troubles of the world.

items.description: Praying draws us near to Heavenly Father, and He strengthens us to carry our burdens.
items.quote: When we pray to our Heavenly Father, we draw near to Him and seek His help, guidance, and blessings.

items.description: This sacred ordinance strengthens our relationship with the Savior and gradually reshapes our lives.
items.quote: The sacrament is a sacred ordinance that strengthens our relationship with the Savior.

items.description: Covenants bind us to God, and the temple helps us stay on the covenant path.
items.quote: Covenants create a bond between us and God, and staying on the covenant path brings the promised blessings that come with that bond.

lists.skip: Four names offered as examples of prayer, with nothing told of each; describing them would go beyond the talk.

lists.principle: In the sacrament we renew simple promises, and keeping them through the week gradually refines our lives.

items.description: We promise to take the name of Jesus Christ upon ourselves.
items.quote: During the sacrament we make promises to take upon us the name of Jesus Christ

items.description: We promise to keep the Savior in mind throughout the week.
items.quote: As we remember Jesus Christ throughout the week

items.description: We promise to obey Him, and striving to do so reshapes who we are.
items.quote: strive to keep His commandments, our lives are gradually refined and reshaped.

24giuffra.brief: Elder Giuffra teaches that tithing is a law of faith with no exceptions, and that as we keep it out of love for God, the Lord fulfills His promises in His own time and way.

lists.principle: Even someone with almost nothing is invited to the blessings of tithing; there are no exceptions to this commandment.

items.description: Her work cleaning and washing barely paid for the single room she shared with her son.
items.quote: What I earn is barely enough to pay the rent for the room where we live

items.description: She could afford only a small amount of wood to keep them warm.
items.quote: buy a small amount of firewood to keep us warm

items.description: What was left bought a little food, and she could not see how tithing would fit.
items.quote: and provide some food. I don’t think I will ever be able to live the law of tithing

lists.principle: We keep the commandments because we love God, and He gives them to bless us.

items.thing: Draw us closer to the Savior
items.description: Commandments bring us nearer to Jesus Christ.
items.quote: Commandments are given to draw us closer to the Savior

items.description: Commandments shield us from harm.
items.quote: to protect us

items.description: Commandments help us stay free from sin and from many of the world's challenges.
items.quote: to help us remain free from sin and many of the challenges the world presents.

lists.skip: Four bare nouns naming trials, with nothing said of each.

lists.principle: The Lord blesses faithful tithe payers, temporally and spiritually.

items.description: He has seen the Lord open the way to work for those who pay their tithing.
items.quote: I have also witnessed the Lord open doors for employment

items.description: He has seen the Lord make education possible.
items.quote: provide education

items.description: He has seen marriages grow stronger.
items.quote: strengthen marriages

items.description: He has seen the Lord fill faithful hearts with peace and hope.
items.quote: and fill faithful hearts with peace and hope.

25morgan.brief: Elder Morgan teaches that the power of God in covenants reaches across generations, so no loved one wanders beyond its reach and no family's story is finished.

lists.skip: Two remembered phrases, given to show the words mattered less than his mother's example.

lists.principle: No time or effort spent reading the Book of Mormon is ever wasted, for anyone.

items.description: Your own reading of the Book of Mormon is never wasted.
items.quote: No time or effort is ever wasted in reading the Book of Mormon. Not for you

items.description: His mother read it aloud to him every day, and he came to know it was true.
items.quote: Even as a single mother, she made the extraordinary effort to read the Book of Mormon to me every day until it was finished.

items.description: Reading it blesses a whole family.
items.quote: not for your family

items.description: There is no one for whom reading it is wasted.
items.quote: not for anyone.

lists.principle: While we wait on God for a struggling loved one, we do our part and trust Him to answer in His own time and way.

items.description: We stay true to the covenants that carry God's power.
items.quote: Keep your covenants

items.description: We keep trying to be faithful ourselves.
items.quote: strive to be faithful

items.thing: Cheerfully do all in your power
items.description: We do what we can with good cheer, then stand still and trust God to show His arm.
items.quote: cheerfully do all things that lie in [your] power; and then may [you] stand still, with the utmost assurance, to see the salvation of God

26fale.brief: Elder Fale teaches that we are children of a Heavenly Father whose love we cannot earn or lose, and that understanding His love draws us to Jesus Christ, frees us from the world's labels and assures us there is still time.

lists.principle: Scripture teaches God's love in terms of the family, from its opening pages.

items.description: It opens with a young family and a baby born in Bethlehem.
items.quote: The New Testament begins with a young family and a baby born in Bethlehem.

items.description: It opens with a family's journey of faith.
items.quote: The Book of Mormon begins with a family’s journey of faith

items.description: It teaches that the Creation was not complete until God had organized a family.
items.quote: the Old Testament teaches how the Creation was not complete until God had organized a family.

lists.principle: Heavenly Father's love is not earned and cannot be lost; it reaches across our whole existence.

items.description: His love came before we had done anything to earn it.
items.quote: He loved you before you were born

items.description: We are His children, and He loves us now.
items.quote: You are His child and He loves you.

items.description: His love remains, so no matter what happens we can always turn back to Him.
items.quote: no matter what has happened, you can always come home, just as you can always turn to your Father in Heaven.

lists.skip: Six bare family roles in one phrase; the point is simply that any family love can teach of the Father's love.

lists.principle: God's love is real, but the adversary twists it into the lie that we can be saved no matter what we choose.

items.description: The lie says His love overlooks our pride.
items.quote: regardless of our pride

items.description: The lie says His love overlooks our rebellion against Him.
items.quote: regardless of our rebellion

items.description: The lie says our sins do not matter because God loves us.
items.quote: regardless of our sins

items.description: The lie says we can turn from Christ and His servants, but receiving Him through covenants is the only way.
items.quote: regardless of our rejection of His Son and His Son’s servants

lists.principle: Knowing how much our Father loves us changes how we see the Savior, ourselves and others.

items.description: We see why the Savior did what He did and loves us as He does, and we want to join His work.
items.quote: First, understanding our Father’s love helps us better understand Jesus Christ.

items.description: We see ourselves and all God's children as beloved and divine, not by the labels the world assigns.
items.quote: we become immune to the divisive and misleading labels of our fallen world

items.description: We reject the lie that it is too late, because there is still time if we turn to Christ.
items.quote: our Father’s message, through His Son, has always been that there is still yet time if we turn to Christ today.

lists.principle: It is never too late in the Father's plan; the claim that it is comes from a pernicious lie.

items.description: The lie says some people can no longer change.
items.quote: it is too late for someone to change

items.thing: Too late to turn to Christ
items.description: The lie says some have gone too far to turn to the Savior.
items.quote: too late for someone to turn to Christ

items.description: The lie says His redeeming grace is out of reach.
items.quote: too late to receive His redeeming grace

lists.principle: In every part of His ministry, Jesus Christ points us to eternal life and shows us the Father's love.

items.description: Even before His birth, the Savior's ministry pointed us to eternal life and the Father's love.
items.quote: Jesus Christ, through His premortal, mortal, and current ministry, points us to eternal life

items.description: While on earth, He taught us to pray to our Father, a loving Father to us all.
items.quote: While still a mortal, He taught us to pray to “our Father.”

items.description: Today He shows the Father's love through priesthood keys held by living prophets and apostles.
items.quote: Today Christ shows us our Father’s love through priesthood keys held by living prophets and apostles.

27kearon.brief: Elder Kearon teaches, from his days learning to glide, that the Savior loves to lift us, and that we live in spiritual lift by feeling for the Spirit, climbing with others and turning away from sink.

lists.principle: Soaring comes only after the basics are learned, one step at a time.

items.description: His first lesson was simply to keep the glider steady.
items.quote: First I learned to fly “straight and level,”

items.description: Next he learned to turn without losing control.
items.quote: then to make stable turns

items.thing: Take off behind a tug plane
items.description: Then he learned to launch while towed into the air.
items.quote: next to take off towed by a tug plane

items.description: Finally he learned to bring the glider safely home, and only then could he learn to climb and soar.
items.quote: and finally to land safely back at the airfield. Only then was I ready to learn to stay in the air, climb, and eventually soar

lists.principle: Rising in lift is quiet and beautiful, much like the feeling of being drawn upward toward our Heavenly Father.

items.description: With no engine, the only steady sound is the wind.
items.quote: with only the whistle of the wind

items.description: Now and then the light aircraft creaks around him.
items.quote: the occasional creak from the glider

items.description: Above all is the magnificent feeling of being lifted by an unseen force.
items.quote: the magnificent sensation of being drawn upward!

lists.principle: The Savior loves to lift, and the scriptures show Him lifting people out of despair.

items.description: He lifted Peter when he began to sink.
items.quote: He lifted His beloved Peter from sinking in the waves

items.description: He lifted Jairus's daughter from death itself.
items.quote: He lifted the daughter of Jairus from the depths of death

items.description: After healing the boy of an unclean spirit, He took him by the hand and raised him.
items.quote: Jesus took him by the hand, and lifted him up.

lists.principle: Living in spiritual lift is not complicated; it comes from simple habits that keep us turning toward the Savior.

items.description: Learn from someone who knows where spiritual lift is found.
items.quote: Find a faithful guide and learn from them where lift is found.

items.description: Pay attention to the sweet feelings of the Holy Spirit and what leads you to them.
items.quote: Actively tune in to the sweet feelings of the Holy Spirit and the things in your life that lead you there.

items.description: Rise alongside others who are already finding lift.
items.quote: Join those who are climbing.

items.description: Follow the practices of those who are rising spiritually.
items.quote: Do what they do.

items.thing: Watch for sink and turn away
items.description: Notice the subtle signs of spiritual decline and turn from them decisively.
items.quote: Watch closely for the subtle signs of sink in your own life, and turn away decisively.

items.thing: Show someone else how to rise
items.description: When you find lift, help others find it too.
items.quote: And when you find lift yourself, show someone else where and how to rise!

items.thing: Soar in the joy of the Lord
items.description: Then rise and rejoice in the Lord.
items.quote: Then soar in the joy of the Lord!

28dunn.brief: Elder Dunn teaches that the Savior carries our burdens, rescuing us not by shortening our course but by helping us lengthen our stride and sending others to help us finish.

lists.skip: Three adjectives in one phrase, with nothing said of each.
Three bare nouns naming the race's hardships; story detail rather than a teaching list.

lists.principle: God helps us finish our race in different ways, and most often by strengthening us to keep going.

items.description: Sometimes God works a great miracle and makes the impossible possible.
items.quote: sometimes the God who makes the impossible possible can part seas and move mountains.

items.description: Other times He sends a friend who believes in us and quietly carries part of our load.
items.quote: Other times He simply sends us a Ted.

items.description: Most often He refills our courage, capacity and confidence so we can run the race before us.
items.quote: But most often He tops off our courage, capacity, and confidence by empowering us to “lay aside every weight”

lists.skip: Repeats the third item of c-12 as three bare nouns.

29eyring.brief: Elder Eyring teaches that all of us meet burdens we cannot carry alone, and that the Savior comforts us through the Holy Ghost while rescuing us from permanent misery.

lists.principle: Self-reliance is good, but it can hide the truth that we will all meet burdens we cannot carry ourselves.

items.description: From a young age we learn to fix what goes wrong.
items.quote: We are trained from a young age to solve problems

items.description: We learn to manage on our own.
items.quote: to be independent

items.description: We learn to keep going and bounce back, yet some burdens are still beyond us.
items.quote: to have perseverance and resilience. But our apparent self-reliance masks a deeper reality

lists.principle: Our burdens differ, but each of us can turn to the Savior, who knows exactly how we feel.

items.description: Some worry about having enough to feed themselves and their families.
items.quote: I know that some of you worry about having enough food each day for you and your family.

items.description: All of us face limits of physical or emotional health, our own or our loved ones'.
items.quote: All of us face eventual limitations of physical or emotional health or the health of loved ones.

items.description: We mourn when people close to us leave the gospel path.
items.quote: We mourn when those close to us stray from the gospel path.

items.description: We can be wounded by someone we love, or grieve the pain we have caused them.
items.quote: We can be hurt by someone we love or hurt by the pain we have caused someone we love.

items.description: We may feel unseen or deeply alone.
items.quote: We may feel misunderstood or deeply lonely.

items.description: We may struggle with a habit we have tried again and again to break.
items.quote: We might have a bad habit we’ve tried to overcome repeatedly without success.

lists.skip: Three bare nouns in one phrase, with nothing said of each.

lists.principle: Even as He comforts us in passing trials, the Savior has rescued us from the only two things that could make us miserable forever.

items.description: Through the Resurrection, death will not keep us apart from our bodies forever.
items.quote: He spares us from the only two things that can bring us permanent misery: separation from our bodies

items.thing: Separation from God because of sin
items.description: Through His sacrifice, sin need not keep us from God forever.
items.quote: separation from God because of sin. Even as He comforts us through temporary times of challenge and pain, He has prepared our rescue from permanent tragedy.

210rasband.brief: Elder Rasband teaches those who grieve for wayward loved ones to turn their despair over to Jesus Christ and to keep loving as He loves, because love is what draws people home.

lists.principle: This message is for everyone whose heart aches for loved ones who have strayed from the Lord.

items.description: Some loved ones have turned from the Lord Himself.
items.quote: loved ones who have turned away from the Lord

items.description: Some have stopped living God's laws.
items.quote: stepped away from obedience to God’s laws

items.description: Some have broken the covenants they made.
items.quote: breached their covenants

items.description: Their choices have left a string of hurting hearts.
items.quote: and left behind a string of broken hearts

lists.skip: Three bare question words, with nothing said of each.
Eight one-word efforts in a single run; the point is that pressure fails, not each verb.

lists.principle: The adversary's deceit leads only to confusion and misery; he has nothing lasting to offer.

items.description: He cannot promise eternal life.
items.quote: He can promise no life eternal

items.thing: No life with God the Father
items.description: He cannot bring anyone home to Heavenly Father.
items.quote: no life with God the Father

items.description: He cannot give peace, now or ever.
items.quote: and no peace. Not now. Not ever!

lists.principle: Love, not pressure, is what can positively influence those who have strayed.

items.description: Love takes a real interest in their lives, their successes and their struggles.
items.quote: Love is being interested in their lives, their successes, and their challenges.

items.description: Love is there for them, welcoming and cheerful.
items.quote: Love is being there with arms outstretched and a cheerful countenance.

items.description: Love lifts them with faith and hope in the Savior.
items.quote: Love is lifting with faith and hope in our Lord and Savior.

items.description: Love leans on the calming influence of the Spirit.
items.quote: Love relies upon the calming influence of the Holy Ghost.

items.description: Love prays for them, as Alma prayed for his son.
items.quote: Love is expressed in prayer.

lists.skip: Five single words describing holiness, with nothing said of each.

lists.principle: Those who grieve for wayward loved ones can find rest by trusting the Savior and never giving up on love.

items.thing: Let go of guilt and never give up
items.description: We fail only when we stop trying, so we keep loving and praying for them.
items.quote: First, let go of any guilt. We fail only when we give up and stop trying, so never, never give up on those you love.

items.description: A person to be loved always matters more than a problem to be solved.
items.quote: Never let a problem to be solved become more important than a person to be loved.

items.description: We seek Him through scripture, the words of His servants and mighty prayer.
items.quote: Third, remember Jesus Christ is the answer. He is, always has been, and always will be.

41eyring.brief: President Eyring testifies that the Lord’s promise, “Fear not, I am with thee,” is true, not by removing our trials but by succoring us in them, often through faithful disciples He sends to help.

lists.principle: The Lord’s succor reaches us in every condition of life, whatever our days may demand.

items.description: Whether our bodies are strong or failing, His help is promised.
items.quote: In ev’ry condition—in sickness, in health,

items.description: Whether we have little or much, the promise holds.
items.quote: In poverty’s vale or abounding in wealth,

items.description: Wherever we are, near or far from home, He is with us.
items.quote: At home or abroad,

items.description: No place lies beyond the reach of His aid.
items.quote: on the land or the sea—

lists.principle: The Lord keeps His promise to succor His children largely through disciples who answer His call to help.

items.thing: Pray to know whom to help
items.description: Members pray to know who needs them and reach out, showing that the Lord knows and loves that person.
items.quote: You have prayed in faith consistently for your family members or friends to know who the Lord would have you help for Him.

items.description: Even a few seconds of kindness or a warm smile can strengthen a missionary’s faith that the Lord is watching over them.
items.quote: Many of you have recognized a discouraged missionary as an invitation to lift a servant of Jesus Christ.

items.description: Showing confidence in those who serve helps them feel that God called them and guides them.
items.quote: You are an important part of the Lord’s answers to their prayers for assurance.

items.thing: Comfort those who plead for it
items.description: We invite the Holy Ghost to show us ways to help the Lord comfort those in need.
items.quote: Another great opportunity can come when you invite the Holy Ghost to help you find ways to help the Lord comfort those who are pleading for it.

lists.principle: Those who come into the fold of God promise to carry one another through trials, as the Lord carries us.

items.description: We help carry what others carry so that their load may be lighter.
items.quote: are willing to bear one another’s burdens, that they may be light;

items.description: We share in others’ grief rather than standing apart from it.
items.quote: willing to mourn with those that mourn;

items.thing: Comfort those in need of comfort
items.description: We offer the comfort the Lord wants His children to receive.
items.quote: yea, and comfort those that stand in need of comfort.

42chibota.brief: Sister Chibota teaches that, like the Savior, we can truly see each person as a beloved child of God, and that this eternal identity matters far more than any worldly label.

lists.skip: Four nouns for what greetings carry; the talk unpacks the idea in the sawubona list instead.

lists.principle: To truly see someone is to acknowledge their worth as a child of God.

items.description: The greeting tells a person they are noticed, not passed by.
items.quote: I recognize you.

items.description: It honors the other person’s worth and humanity.
items.quote: I respect you.

items.description: It says the person counts, more than a simple hello can.
items.quote: You matter.

lists.principle: Where others saw labels, the Savior saw beloved sons and daughters of God.

items.description: The Savior truly saw her as she was, a daughter of God.
items.quote: He saw the woman at the well,

items.description: One others kept away from, He saw and did not pass by.
items.quote: the leper,

items.description: He saw the man who could not see Him.
items.quote: the blind man,

items.description: Even the smallest among the people had His full attention.
items.quote: and the child.

lists.skip: Six example worldly labels with one shared point; nothing to say item by item.

lists.principle: Our identity as a child of God is inherited, so it holds steady through anything life brings.

items.description: A new situation, good or hard, does not change who we are.
items.quote: That eternal identity does not change when circumstances change,

items.description: Our mistakes do not undo our divine worth.
items.quote: when we make mistakes,

items.description: How others see us cannot change how God sees us.
items.quote: or when others misunderstand us.

lists.principle: Seeing others as God sees them begins with small, deliberate acts this week.

items.description: Helping someone feel seen can start with learning the name of one who may feel unseen.
items.quote: Learn the name of someone who may feel unseen.

items.thing: Pray to see as He sees
items.description: We ask Heavenly Father to help us see others as He does.
items.quote: Pray to see others as Heavenly Father sees them.

items.description: We put eternal truths in the place of the labels the world uses.
items.quote: Replace worldly labels with these eternal truths:

lists.principle: Three eternal truths describe who we really are, in place of the world’s labels.

items.description: Before anything else, we are spirit children of our Heavenly Father.
items.quote: Child of God.

items.description: We belong to God through the covenants we make with Him.
items.quote: Child of the covenant.

items.description: We follow the Savior, who sees who we are and who we can become.
items.quote: Disciple of Jesus Christ.

lists.principle: Heavenly Father and Jesus Christ know each of us completely and personally.

items.description: They know you individually, by name.
items.quote: They know your name,

items.description: They know what you are passing through.
items.quote: your circumstances,

items.description: They know the gifts you have been given.
items.quote: your gifts,

items.description: The Savior sees not only who you are but who you can become.
items.quote: He sees not only who we are but who we can become.

43andersen.brief: Elder Andersen teaches that faith in Jesus Christ gives us spiritual courage to choose the right, and that as we act with courage, our faith in Christ grows stronger.

lists.principle: Discipleship is not a casual pursuit; it takes spiritual courage to triumph over obstacles, doubt and fear.

items.description: Following the Savior fully has always taken courage born of faith.
items.quote: Being His true disciple,

items.description: Disciples rise above the pull of the world around them.
items.quote: overcoming the world,

items.description: Choosing the right, even when it is hard, is part of discipleship.
items.quote: keeping His commandments,

items.description: We trust the Savior and what He has promised, whatever comes.
items.quote: and trusting in Him and His promises are not casual pursuits.

lists.skip: Three alliterative nouns for the challenges of our day; the talk does not treat them one by one.
A rhetorical triad about what our phones bring; not a list to unpack.

lists.principle: Faith in Jesus Christ gives us the spiritual courage to live His gospel in everyday choices and to trust Him when life is upended.

items.description: Faith gives us courage to reach out and care for others.
items.quote: It is our faith in Jesus Christ that brings the spiritual courage to minister to others,

items.description: We keep the Lord’s law of health with courage.
items.quote: live the Word of Wisdom,

items.description: We stay morally clean, as the Lord asks.
items.quote: keep the law of chastity,

items.description: We keep the Lord’s day holy.
items.quote: honor the Sabbath day,

items.description: We pay an honest tithe in faith.
items.quote: be honest in our tithing,

items.description: When illness, money troubles or disaster strike, faith lets us keep trusting the Father and the Son.
items.quote: trust our Father and His Son when unforeseen illness, financial troubles, or natural disaster upend our life.

lists.principle: The faith of young men and women around the world gives them courage to take each step of discipleship.

items.description: Young people rise before the sun to learn the gospel.
items.quote: the courage to get up before the sun rises to attend seminary

items.description: They go out to serve the Lord.
items.quote: and then to serve missions

items.description: After returning, they marry and start families, and those not able to marry stay true to their covenants.
items.quote: upon returning, to marry and begin a family

lists.principle: Faith in Christ also gives us courage to share our witness, make covenants and follow the Lord’s guidance.

items.description: We find courage to talk with others about Jesus Christ.
items.quote: speak openly with others about our Savior,

items.description: We make covenants in the house of the Lord.
items.quote: make covenants in the house of the Lord,

items.description: We have courage to repent and receive the Lord’s forgiveness.
items.quote: repent and receive forgiveness,

items.description: We follow those the Lord has called to lead today.
items.quote: follow living prophets,

items.thing: Be guided by the Holy Ghost
items.description: We act on the quiet impressions of the Spirit.
items.quote: and be guided by the quiet impressions of the Holy Ghost.

44fantone.brief: Elder Fantone teaches that we do not simply add the Savior’s name to our own; we take His name upon us by covenant and a lifelong determination to serve Him by serving others.

lists.principle: Taking the Savior’s name means serving others, even when it costs us our own space and comfort.

items.description: His parents gave it to a former student who could not afford housing near his school.
items.quote: my parents opened our home and offered him the boys’ room.

items.description: Children from a vulnerable family, whom the Relief Society president told them of, moved in.
items.quote: some of the children indefinitely moved into our sisters’ room.

items.description: He believes his parents would have given even their own room to Joseph and Mary.
items.quote: my parents would have gladly offered their room.

lists.principle: Missionaries who served even while homesick were changed by their service.

items.description: Sad and lonely, they turned first to prayer.
items.quote: Yet these valiant missionaries got on their knees,

items.description: They put on the name of Jesus Christ they carried.
items.quote: put on their name tags,

items.description: They served despite their feelings, and in time they changed.
items.quote: and went out to serve anyway.

lists.skip: The scriptural phrase “heart, might, mind, and strength” describes wholeness, not four separate teachings.

lists.principle: We serve the Savior by serving the people around us.

items.description: Helping others rise, as his parents helped a student fulfill his potential.
items.quote: Desiring to help him fulfill his potential, my parents opened our home

items.description: Service turned homesick missionaries into missionaries who loved the people.
items.quote: I love the people, and I love this work.

items.description: Serving others is how we serve God.
items.quote: When ye are in the service of your fellow beings ye are only in the service of your God

45dube.brief: Elder Dube teaches that we do not need to perfect ourselves before coming to Christ; we come to Him as we are, with a willing heart, to be perfected.

lists.principle: Moroni’s invitation to come unto Christ asks us to act, let go, and come as we are so He can perfect us.

items.description: Coming is an action: we choose to move from where we are to a better place.
items.quote: Come: It’s an action. We choose to move from our current place to a better place.

items.description: We surrender and let go of what is holding us back.
items.quote: Deny yourselves: Surrender. Let go of the things that are holding us back.

items.description: We come with a willing heart, and He gives us a new heart.
items.quote: Be perfected in Him: Come as we are with a willing heart. He will give us a new heart.

lists.principle: We come to Christ not by first making ourselves perfect but by doing the best we can and turning to Him.

items.description: Brother Child and his wife turned to the Lord in prayer.
items.quote: We left after kneeling in prayer.

items.description: He trusted the Lord to help him.
items.quote: I had trust in the Lord.

items.description: He came willing, and the Savior’s grace helped him let go of what held him back.
items.quote: The Savior, through His grace, helped him to let go of what was holding him back.

lists.skip: Seven nouns naming whatever may hold us back; the talk’s point is the whole set, not each item.

lists.principle: The invitation to come unto Christ passes from scripture to each of us, to live it ourselves.

items.description: Moroni invited all to come unto Christ and be perfected in Him.
items.quote: Yea, come unto Christ, and be perfected in him

items.description: In answer to her prayer, Sister Child learned her husband did not need to be perfect.
items.quote: Randall doesn’t need to be perfect. He needs to do the very best he can.

items.description: Brother Child came to Christ as he was and was sealed in the temple.
items.quote: Randall didn’t perfect himself to come to Christ.

items.description: If we do not deny His power, we are sanctified in Christ by His grace.
items.quote: You too can live it. If you will “deny not his power, then are ye sanctified in Christ by the grace of God

46cook.brief: Elder Cook teaches that integrity, virtue and happiness are linked in the Father’s plan, and that living with integrity and virtue, with ongoing repentance, keeps us on the covenant path.

lists.skip: A four-word list from Preach My Gospel that the talk quotes without unpacking.

lists.principle: In the Father’s plan, living with integrity and virtue leads to true happiness.

items.description: Integrity is the willingness and ability to live by our beliefs and commitments.
items.quote: integrity (the willingness and ability to live by our beliefs and commitments) is one of the foundation stones of good character

items.description: A virtuous life aligns us with God’s will.
items.quote: Living a virtuous life with integrity aligns us with God’s will.

items.description: True happiness is the outcome of integrity and virtue.
items.quote: True happiness, often translated as blessedness, is the actual outcome of integrity and being virtuous.

lists.skip: Six qualities named in one sentence that the talk does not unpack one by one.
President McKay’s five qualities, named in one line and not unpacked.

lists.principle: Through repentance and the ordinances of the gospel, we can be forgiven and feel deep joy.

items.description: The sailor said learning of repentance felt like stepping onto the earth of home again.
items.quote: He compared repentance to the feelings he had when he arrived back in England

items.description: Before his baptism he prayed to share his joy with others, especially his family.
items.quote: Just before his baptism, he prayed to the Lord to help him that he might be able to give other people the same joy

items.description: With repentance and baptism, confirmation completed the way to forgiveness he learned of.
items.quote: through repentance, baptism, and confirmation he could receive forgiveness

lists.principle: In a coarse and challenging world, integrity, virtue and ongoing repentance are the answer.

items.description: We show integrity by living virtuous lives and caring for and serving others.
items.quote: We show our integrity by living virtuous lives and caring for and serving others.

items.description: The ultimate reward of integrity and virtue is the constant companionship of the Holy Ghost.
items.quote: The ultimate reward of integrity and virtue is the constant companionship of the Holy Ghost.

items.description: Making repentance a daily part of life lets us approach the Lord with integrity.
items.quote: When we make repentance a constant, day-to-day part of our lives, we can approach the Lord with integrity

47kyungu.brief: Elder Kyungu takes up President Oaks’s invitation to use the language of peacemakers, naming hurtful words to forgo and peaceful words to use in their place.

lists.principle: From ancient times the Lord has warned against speech that creates conflict.

items.description: Speaking falsehood is among the things the Lord hates.
items.quote: a lying tongue,

items.description: Bearing false witness against another is an abomination to Him.
items.quote: a false witness that speaketh lies,

items.description: Stirring up strife among brothers and sisters is also named.
items.quote: he that soweth discord among brethren.

lists.skip: A list of people who may have hurt us with words; it sets up the talk rather than teaching item by item.

lists.principle: Some words damage relationships and never edify; disciples of Jesus Christ forgo them.

items.description: Tells a person they have no worth.
items.quote: You are useless.

items.description: An insult that humiliates and degrades.
items.quote: You are stupid.

items.description: Sweeps away every good effort with one word.
items.quote: You never do anything right.

items.description: Questions a person’s worth rather than the problem.
items.quote: What is wrong with you?

items.description: Puts the whole fault on one person.
items.quote: This is all your fault.

items.description: Turns one mistake into a label.
items.quote: You always mess things up.

items.description: Accuses rather than seeking to be understood.
items.quote: You never listen.

items.description: Places blame instead of working toward a solution.
items.quote: You caused this problem.

items.description: Shuts the other person out.
items.quote: Leave me alone.

items.description: Signals indifference to what matters to another.
items.quote: I do not care.

items.description: Tells someone they have no place in our life.
items.quote: I do not need you in my life.

items.thing: I do not care about you
items.description: Denies love to the person in front of us.
items.quote: I do not care about you.

items.description: Silences someone instead of hearing them.
items.quote: Just stop talking.

items.description: Tells a person they are a burden.
items.quote: I am tired of you.

lists.principle: Harsh words do real harm to the people and relationships we care about.

items.description: Harsh words wear away the love between people.
items.quote: They weaken love,

items.description: They lower the respect we hold for one another.
items.quote: diminish respect,

items.description: They harm the bonds that hold families and friends together.
items.quote: and damage relationships.

lists.principle: In place of contention, peacemakers choose words that build understanding, strengthen confidence and preserve relationships.

items.description: A simple courtesy that shows respect.
items.quote: Please.

items.description: Gratitude spoken aloud.
items.quote: Thank you.

items.description: Notices and values what another has done.
items.quote: I appreciate that.

items.description: Honors another’s opinion even when it differs.
items.quote: I respect your view.

items.description: Acknowledges what is right in what someone says.
items.quote: This is a good point.

items.description: Calms a heated moment and opens conversation.
items.quote: Let us slow down and talk.

items.quote: We can work this out.

items.description: Reassures and lowers the tension.
items.quote: It is OK.

items.description: Invites both people to keep their peace.
