48schmeil.brief: Elder Schmeil teaches that the Savior and our covenants are divine helps on the path home, and invites us, as the Lord invited ancient Israel, to consider our ways so He can bless us.

lists.principle: God did not leave us alone in mortality; He gave us divine helps to bring us back to His presence.

items.description: He knows us individually and, as we come to Him in humility and faith, makes weak things strong.
items.quote: Jesus Christ knows us individually, and He will help us if we seek Him

items.description: Through covenants we are yoked with the Savior and our burdens become lighter.
items.quote: It is through covenants that we become yoked with the Savior Jesus Christ and our burdens become lighter.

49oaks.brief: President Oaks teaches that the gospel of Jesus Christ is for all people, and invites each of us, whatever our doubts, to draw closer to the Savior through faith, humility and covenants.

lists.principle: God, who knows all truth, expects us to learn by both science and the Spirit; there is no ultimate conflict between them.

items.description: Knowledge from science and digital information keeps evolving and may be inaccurate.
items.quote: the evolving disclosures of man through the scientific method and digital information, which may be inaccurate

items.description: Truth discovered by the Spirit begins with faith in God and relies on scripture, inspired teaching and revelation.
items.quote: the truths discovered through the spiritual method, which begins with faith in God and relies on scriptures, inspired teaching, and personal revelation

51uchtdorf.brief: President Uchtdorf teaches that baptism makes us part of a covenant people, and that as we center our lives on Jesus Christ He draws us closer to Him and to each other in a unity the world cannot give.

lists.principle: Baptism is a personal promise to follow the Savior, made in three simple commitments.

items.thing: Take upon us the Savior’s name
items.description: At baptism we promise to carry His name as His followers.
items.quote: made sacred covenants to take upon themselves the Savior’s name

items.description: We promise to live by what God has asked of us.
items.quote: keep God’s commandments

items.description: We promise to give our lives to His service.
items.quote: and serve Him

lists.principle: Spiritual growth starts small, but each step along the covenant path multiplies our capacity for divine understanding and blessings.

items.description: Receiving the endowment in the house of the Lord deepens our relationship with God.
items.quote: The temple endowment

items.description: Serving a mission is one of the experiences that multiplies our discipleship rather than merely adding to it.
items.quote: missionary service

items.description: Being married in the house of the Lord expands our capacity for a joyful life.
items.quote: celestial marriage in the house of the Lord

items.description: Continuing to serve in the Church keeps the arc of discipleship rising toward the Savior.
items.quote: ongoing service in God’s kingdom

lists.principle: At baptism we declare that we do not want to live only for ourselves but to belong to a people who care for one another.

items.description: We help carry the loads that others are carrying.
items.quote: bear one another’s burdens

items.description: We stay close to others in their sorrow and grieve with them.
items.quote: mourn with those that mourn

items.description: We offer comfort to anyone who needs it.
items.quote: comfort those that stand in need of comfort

lists.skip: Three adverbs (culturally, politically, religiously) describing how the ancient world was divided; scene-setting, not a list to learn from.

lists.principle: Jesus Christ reached across every worldly boundary to gather those others shunned as outsiders, and He still invites all to come unto Him.

items.description: He reached out physically to people others kept away from.
items.quote: He touched lepers.

items.description: He honored the faith of people His culture considered unclean.
items.quote: He praised Gentiles for their faith.

items.description: He held up a Samaritan, from a people Jews avoided, as the model of compassion.
items.quote: He used a Samaritan as an example of compassion.

items.description: He called people of very different backgrounds to serve side by side in positions of trust.
items.quote: He gathered people from different walks of life and asked them to serve together in positions of trust.

items.description: He ministered to people whatever their means.
items.quote: He ministered to the poor and rich alike.

lists.principle: The Savior chose leaders for His Church from very different backgrounds and asked them to serve together.

items.description: Peter and Andrew were working fishermen when He called them.
items.quote: The Savior called fishermen like Peter and Andrew

items.description: Matthew, a tax collector, was among those the Savior called to lead.
items.quote: a tax collector like Matthew

items.description: Paul, a Pharisee, was also called to lead His Church.
items.quote: a Pharisee like Paul to lead His Church

lists.skip: Three single nouns (contention, mistrust, hatred) naming the fruits of Satan’s dividing work in passing; the sentence carries the point.

lists.principle: People unite around many things, often with strong feelings, but none of these is what makes the Savior’s people one.

items.description: Some groups form around social causes or political ideas.
items.quote: Some have united over social causes or political ideas.

items.description: Some come together to celebrate where they come from.
items.quote: Some unite to celebrate their cultural heritage.

items.description: Sadly, some unite only in shared hostility toward others.
items.quote: Some, sadly, have united because of hatred for another group.

items.description: Others gather around interests, work, or even a favorite team or soft drink.
items.quote: Others unite around hobbies, professional interests, or even love for a favorite soccer team or brand of soft drink.

lists.principle: In the Savior’s Church, what unites us is not politics, culture or interests, but our love and our covenants.

items.description: We are drawn together by loving God and loving His children around us.
items.quote: It is our love for God and neighbor, God’s children.

items.description: We are bound together by our covenants with Jesus Christ and our devotion to His restored gospel.
items.quote: It is our commitment to our covenants with Jesus Christ and to His restored gospel.

lists.principle: Small, steady changes in how we treat others leave less room for pride and contention, and make way for Christ-centered unity.

items.description: We give others more time and grace.
items.quote: a little more patient

items.description: We add a little more kindness to how we treat people.
items.quote: a little kinder

items.description: We let go of offenses more readily.
items.quote: more forgiving

items.description: We look for ways to lend a hand.
items.quote: more helpful

items.description: We reach out to those who live and worship around us.
items.quote: more neighborly

52munoz-spannaus.brief: Sister Muñoz Spannaus teaches young women that the Lord knows exactly where they are and loves them perfectly, and that with Him at their side they can pursue their righteous aspirations and the work He has for them.

lists.principle: The Lord knows each of us completely, and knowing everything about us does not make Him love us less.

items.description: He knows what you hope for and what you have been given.
items.quote: He knows your dreams and your gifts.

items.description: He knows when you feel alone and what you are wondering about.
items.quote: He knows when you feel alone and what your questions are.

items.description: He knows what you face and how to turn your weaknesses into strengths.
items.quote: He knows your challenges and how to turn your weaknesses into strengths.

lists.principle: Each young woman has important work to do on earth, and simple daily habits help her do it with joy; she invites them to choose one to focus on.

items.description: Come to the sacrament grateful for the promise of the Holy Ghost, and ask each morning for His companionship.
items.quote: Partake of the sacrament with a humble heart, grateful for the promise that as you keep your covenants, the Holy Ghost will be your constant companion.

items.description: End each day by asking for forgiveness as you pray.
items.quote: Repent daily and at the end of the day, as you pray, ask for forgiveness.

items.description: Read the scriptures to come to know God, so you can do His will and love Him more.
items.quote: Study the scriptures with a desire to know God’s character so you can do His will, increase your love for Him, and advance His work.

items.description: Learn what it means to have ministering angels help you.
items.quote: Study what it means to have ministering angels help you.

items.description: Go to bed early and sleep enough to keep your mind clear and alert.
items.quote: Protect your sleep; go to bed early. Get enough sleep to keep your mind clear and alert.

items.description: Social media can steal our peace and self-esteem and the real connection that comes face to face.
items.quote: Limit cell phone use. Social media makes us believe we are connected; however, it is a thief of our peace of mind, self-esteem, and the real connection

items.description: Following President Oaks, choose friends who are trying to follow the Lord and strengthen your faith.
items.quote: Seek friends … who are striving to follow the Lord … with whom you can feel the Spirit and … reinforce your faith.

lists.skip: Four single nouns (self-esteem, mind, thoughts, spirit) from a priesthood blessing; the point is the promise that follows, that the Godhead is at your side.

53villanueva.brief: Elder Villanueva teaches that the Lord keeps His promise to open the windows of heaven to those who pay an honest tithe, though His blessings often come in subtle ways we can easily overlook.

lists.principle: Tithing brings significant but subtle blessings, temporal and spiritual, that we see when we take the time to list them.

items.description: He has been able to work and provide for many years.
items.quote: I have enjoyed steady employment for many years.

items.description: His wife, his children and he have been blessed with health.
items.quote: My wife, my children, and I have been blessed with good health.

items.description: What his family owned was kept safe even in hard times.
items.quote: Our home and temporal possessions have been preserved, even during difficult times.

items.description: The Lord helped him manage his time and means so he could get an education.
items.quote: The Lord has blessed me with the ability to manage my time and resources so I could obtain an education.

items.description: He learned to see the Lord’s hand in each tender mercy and to be grateful for it.
items.quote: I have developed the gift of gratitude by learning to appreciate the Lord’s hand in each of His tender mercies.

items.description: He learned to recognize the Spirit’s influence when making important decisions.
items.quote: I have learned to recognize the influence of the Holy Ghost when making important decisions in my life.

54bednar.brief: Elder Bednar teaches that ordinances and covenants are our credentials for returning to God, that they must be kept valid and sealed over time by the Holy Spirit of Promise, and that no faithful covenant keeper will lose a promised blessing because of another person’s choices.

lists.principle: The Holy Ghost, the third member of the Godhead, is the one who confirms our covenants as acceptable to God.

items.description: He is the third member of the Godhead, a personage of spirit.
items.quote: He is a personage of spirit

items.description: He bears witness of what is true.
items.quote: testifies of all truth

items.description: He witnesses of the Father and the Son and carries Their messages to us.
items.quote: is the witness of and messenger for the Father and the Son

lists.principle: The ratifying seal of the Holy Spirit of Promise usually comes not in one moment but over time, as we keep living our covenants.

items.description: We keep turning to God, honestly and steadily, not just once.
items.quote: as we repent sincerely and consistently

items.description: We keep the promises we made in sacred ordinances.
items.quote: honor our covenants

items.description: We give our hearts and wills over to Him.
items.quote: yield our hearts unto God

lists.principle: The temple sealing joins a husband and wife to each other and also to God’s eternal family, and both parts are vital.

items.description: A man and a woman are united to each other in eternal marriage.
items.quote: the eternal union of a man and a woman in marriage—what may be understood as a lateral sealing

items.description: The couple is sealed into God’s eternal family and linked with all generations.
items.quote: the sealing of the husband and wife into God’s eternal family and the linking of humankind through all generations—what may be understood as a vertical sealing

lists.principle: A temple sealing is meant to bless a couple with a lifetime of growth and happiness together.

items.description: A couple grows spiritually across a whole lifetime together.
items.quote: a lifetime of spiritual growth

items.description: Husband and wife are devoted to each other.
items.quote: marital devotion

items.description: They remain loyal and faithful to each other.
items.quote: fidelity

items.description: They work as one through the uncertainties and challenges of life.
items.quote: working together to overcome the uncertainties and challenges of mortality

items.description: Their marriage brings joy that lasts.
items.quote: enduring happiness

lists.principle: Sometimes a spouse’s choices undo what a sealing was meant to bring, yet another person’s unrighteousness can never rob a faithful covenant keeper of God’s promises.

items.description: A spouse’s unrepented sins can wound a marriage.
items.quote: A spouse’s sins

items.description: Breaking the promise of faithfulness can bring alienation.
items.quote: infidelity

items.description: A spouse turning away from the faith can strain the marriage.
items.quote: personal apostasy

items.description: Other troubles may also lead to contention, alienation, and even divorce.
items.quote: or other difficulties may cause contention, alienation, and even divorce

55lebethoa.brief: Elder Lebethoa teaches that Jesus Christ is the light and life of the world, and that through faith nourished by prayer and scripture study, and through repentance, we can receive more of His light in our daily struggles.

lists.skip: Six relationships (spouse, child, family member, friend, colleague, neighbor) named in one clause to set the scene; not a list to learn from.
Four single feelings (anger, disappointment, frustration, regret) named in passing to describe a conversation gone wrong.

lists.principle: Whatever concerns, challenges and struggles we carry, the answer is always Jesus Christ.

items.description: We may worry about being able to provide for ourselves.
items.quote: becoming self-reliant

items.description: We may feel the pressure of what is expected of us in study or employment.
items.quote: meeting the demands placed upon us at school or at work

items.description: We may struggle with feelings that we are not enough, or with fear and doubt.
items.quote: feeling inadequacy, fear, and doubt

items.thing: The loss of a loved one
items.description: We may be grieving someone we love.
items.quote: dealing with the loss of a loved one

items.thing: Knowing what to do with our lives
items.description: We may simply be unsure of our direction.
items.quote: or simply knowing what to do with our lives

lists.principle: We receive more of the Savior’s light by exercising faith in Him and by repenting.

items.description: We trust that He understands our difficulties, nourishing that faith each day with prayer and scripture study.
items.quote: Having faith in Jesus Christ means trusting that He understands our daily difficulties and knows how to help us rise above them

items.description: We change our minds and turn our hearts to God, with the Savior’s help.
items.quote: Repentance means a change of mind and a turning of the heart to God.

lists.principle: There is no single right way to study the scriptures; consistency and sincerity matter more than method, timing or length.

items.description: We can read the scriptures in order from beginning to end.
items.quote: We may choose to read chronologically

items.description: We can follow a subject through the scriptures.
items.quote: study by topic

items.description: We can search the scriptures with a particular question in mind.
items.quote: focus on a particular question

items.thing: Begin with a verse that draws you
items.description: We can start with a passage that catches our attention.
items.quote: begin with a passage or verse that draws our attention

lists.principle: Repentance begins by honestly asking what we need to change, and we do not have to change alone.

items.description: We can ponder whether our days are spent on what matters.
items.quote: how we use our time

items.thing: What we watch or listen to
items.description: We can consider what we let into our minds.
items.quote: the things we watch or listen to

items.description: We can look at how we speak with others.
items.quote: the language and tone we use as we communicate with others

56sinclair.brief: Elder Sinclair teaches that a true disciple of Jesus Christ is quick to help and slow to judge, as the Savior was with the woman at the well, looking not only to people’s past but to their possible.

lists.principle: The Savior ministered one by one, in personal conversations with people of every kind.

items.description: His personal conversation with the Savior is recorded in Matthew 19.
items.quote: the rich young ruler

items.description: Even on the cross, the Savior spoke personally with him, as Luke 23 records.
items.quote: the thief on the cross

items.description: The Savior taught him one on one, as John 3 records.
items.quote: Nicodemus

items.description: The Savior spoke with the man at the pool, as John 5 records.
items.quote: the man at the pool of Bethesda

items.description: The Savior spoke with Pilate face to face, as John 18 records.
items.quote: Pontius Pilate

items.description: The risen Savior spoke with her personally, as John 20 records.
items.quote: Mary Magdalene

items.description: The Savior spoke with Peter one by one, as John 21 records.
items.quote: and Simon Peter

lists.skip: Three rhetorical guesses (widowed? divorced? abandoned?) raised only to say we do not know her circumstances; the lesson is not to judge, not the items.

lists.principle: The Savior helped the woman at the well instead of judging her, looking not only to her past but to her possible.

items.description: He spoke to her in a way that honored her.
items.quote: He spoke to the woman with dignity, not shame.

items.description: He listened to her questions and answered them earnestly.
items.quote: He earnestly listened to her questions and responded with teaching, not ridicule.

items.thing: Not held hostage to her history
items.description: He did not let her past define what she could become.
items.quote: He did not hold her hostage to her history.

items.description: He trusted her with who He was, and she left with a purpose.
items.quote: He trusted her with truth.

lists.skip: The four steps of missionary work (find, teach, baptize, confirm) named in passing; the sentence’s point is the people at modern-day wells.

lists.principle: Being quick to help and slow to judge is a simple, encouraging way to answer the call to be holy.

items.description: Helping instead of judging is how we answer President Oaks’s call to seek holiness.
items.quote: to be more holy

items.description: It makes us more like Jesus Christ, who helped the woman at the well.
items.quote: to be more like our Savior

items.description: It is the mark of a true disciple of Jesus Christ.
items.quote: to be His true disciples

57stevenson.brief: Elder Stevenson teaches children that the gospel is like the sweet fruit of Lehi’s tree of life, and invites them to love, share and invite so others can taste its joy too.

lists.principle: The fruit of the tree of life stands for the blessings that come through the Atonement of Jesus Christ.

items.description: The sacred ordinances of the gospel are among the fruit’s blessings.
items.quote: including ordinances

items.description: The covenants we make with God are part of the fruit.
items.quote: covenants

items.description: Gospel truths become sweet to us as we live them.
items.quote: and truths of the restored gospel

items.description: The fruit points ultimately to eternal life.
items.quote: and ultimately eternal life

lists.principle: Gospel truths are like fruit: we know how sweet they are only once we taste them by living them.

items.description: Knowing we are His children makes us stronger and kinder, since everyone around us is our brother or sister.
items.quote: First, we are children of a loving Heavenly Father.

items.description: God’s plan, centered on the Atonement of Jesus Christ, brings peace and hope, even in grief.
items.quote: Second, the great plan of happiness through Jesus Christ.

items.thing: The gift of the Holy Ghost
items.description: His constant companionship, received after baptism, is a most delicious fruit.
items.quote: Finally, a most delicious fruit for Latter-day Saints is the gift of the Holy Ghost, His constant companionship.

lists.principle: Knowing God’s plan for His children can turn deep grief into peace, joy and hope.

items.description: The grieving priest’s despair gave way to peace when he learned where his wife was.
items.quote: peace for despair

items.description: His sadness was replaced with joy.
items.quote: joy for sadness

items.description: Where there had been only loss, there was hope.
items.quote: hope for ashes

lists.principle: The Holy Ghost, a member of the Godhead, has important roles in our lives.

items.description: The Holy Ghost warns us.
items.quote: His very important roles include to warn

items.description: He comforts us, even in the most difficult of times.
items.quote: inviting the Spirit to comfort and testify to all that we are children of a loving Heavenly Father, even in the most difficult of times

items.description: He whispers truth to us and tells us it is true.
items.quote: The Spirit whispers this to me and tells me it is true

lists.principle: Like Lehi, when we taste the joy of the gospel we want those we love to taste it too, and helping them brings even greater joy.

items.description: Show love for others, in words and actions.
items.quote: Show love for others

items.description: Share the fruits of the gospel with others.
items.quote: share the fruits of the gospel with others

items.description: Invite others to partake of the sweet fruit of the gospel with you.
items.quote: invite others to partake of the sweet fruit of the gospel with you

58reid.brief: Brother Reid teaches that anyone who loves the Master Teacher is good enough to teach His gospel, because the Lord promises to make us into the teachers He needs, and teaching like the Savior means loving like Him.

lists.principle: Many who are asked to teach the gospel feel inadequate and wonder whether they are enough.

items.description: We worry that we lack the knowledge to teach.
items.quote: Do I know enough?

items.description: We wonder whether we are good enough to teach the gospel of Jesus Christ.
items.quote: Am I good enough to teach the gospel of Jesus Christ?

lists.principle: Wherever we teach, the Lord’s promise is the same: He will help us do His work, and we were never meant to do it alone.

items.description: Some of his earliest Primary classes met beneath a mango tree, taught by teachers who loved him.
items.quote: Many of my earliest Primary classes were held beneath the shade of a mango tree.

items.description: As mission leaders, loving the Savior more helped them love those they taught.
items.quote: We learned that the surest way to truly love those we taught was to deepen our love for the One we taught about.

items.description: His parents made their home in American Samoa his first classroom of gospel learning.
items.quote: Our home in the village of Leone, American Samoa, became my first classroom of gospel learning.

items.description: The resurrected Savior began by inviting each person to come to Him individually.
items.quote: He invited each person to come unto Him one by one so they could know for themselves that He was Jesus Christ.

lists.principle: For every gospel teacher, the two great commandments become one simple invitation: love the Lord and love those you teach.

items.description: First, love God with all our heart, soul and mind.
items.quote: to love the Lord our God with all our heart, soul, and mind

items.description: Second, love others as ourselves, which for a teacher means loving those we teach.
items.quote: to love our neighbor as ourselves

lists.principle: For the Master Teacher, love for the people did not end when the lesson ended.

items.description: Filled with compassion, He healed those who were sick.
items.quote: He healed their sick

items.description: He blessed the children of the people He had taught.
items.quote: blessed their children

items.description: He prayed for each of them individually.
items.quote: and prayed for them one by one

lists.principle: We are good enough to teach the gospel not because of our knowledge or skill, but because we can love the Master Teacher.

items.description: Our worthiness to teach does not depend on knowing it all.
items.quote: Not because you know everything.

items.thing: Not because of your teaching skill
items.description: It does not depend on having every teaching skill.
items.quote: Not because you have every teaching skill.

items.description: It does not depend on always feeling capable.
items.quote: Not because you always feel capable or confident.

items.description: It rests on our love for the Savior, who will make us into the teachers He knows we can become.
items.quote: Because you can love the Master Teacher!

lists.principle: Whoever we are and wherever we start, the invitation to come unto the Master Teacher and love Him is the same.

items.description: He jokes that he hopes people think he is one of the scholars named in the headline.
items.quote: I really hope people think I’m one of the scholars!

items.description: The headline about the new presidency mentioned an NFL player.
items.quote: New Sunday School Leaders Include Men Involved in Church Education and an NFL Player

items.description: Those who have followed Christ for many years receive the same invitation.
items.quote: a lifelong disciple

items.description: Those who have only recently begun, or begun again, to follow Christ are invited too.
items.quote: someone who has recently started—or started again—to follow Christ

59gilbert.brief: Elder Gilbert teaches that disciples of Jesus Christ must stand for truth with love, and amplifies five principles from President Oaks for doing both at once.

lists.principle: Truth and love always walk together for disciples of Jesus Christ; standing for truth without love loses the Spirit, and love without truth separates people from God.

items.description: Sometimes the peacemaking choice is to stay quiet, remembering that hostility may hide pain we cannot see.
items.quote: First, avoid overly contentious settings.

items.description: Listening before responding builds common ground from which we can teach with love.
items.quote: Resisting the impulse to initially respond built common ground, which allowed me later to teach from a place of love.

items.description: Keeping our own covenants and loving the Lord openly does more than any argument.
items.quote: Being a light opens more doors than any pointed argument ever will.

items.description: Loving others never means surrendering our values or minimizing God’s laws.
items.quote: When we try to love others by minimizing God’s laws, we separate ourselves from the one person who loves them the very most.

items.description: We check whether we carry His charity, patience and kindness as we stand for truth.
items.quote: The fifth principle then is to stay anchored in Jesus Christ.
